jobs.title: Director, Customer Intelligence
jobs.description:
Reporting to the VP, Advanced Analytics, the Director, Customer Intelligence will develop and execute our Customer Analytics Intake across multiple data analysis teams.

This role will establish a center of practice for how analytics requests enter the organization, establish clear priorities, and coordinate work through delivery.

The role will serve as the operating hub and delivery lead for enterprise customer and commercial analytics. It will bring structure to incoming demand, protect the capacity of specialist teams, and ensure business partners have clear visibility into scope, ownership, timelines, dependencies, and expected outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Own the end-to-end intake process for analytics, BI, measurement, and data requests from the COO and CCO organizations.
Lead a weekly intake forum, maintain a shared prioritization framework, and establish transparent service levels.
Partner with business stakeholders to clarify objectives, define requirements, assess readiness, and agree on expected outcomes.
Evaluate incoming requests and coordinate assignment to the appropriate Customer Analytics, Advanced Analytics, Measurement, or Data Engineering team.
Escalate capacity constraints, competing priorities, and delivery trade-offs requiring leadership decisions.
Establish clear rules of engagement, request templates, governance routines, and a single visible backlog.
Ensure business partners understand the status, owner, next milestone, and expected timing of each request.
Lead planning and delivery coordination
Translate approved requests into clearly defined scope, deliverables, timelines, milestones, and accountabilities.
Coordinate project activities across business, analytics, data, technology, and other enabling teams.
Maintain project plans and track progress against agreed commitments.
Monitor risks, issues, dependencies, scope changes, and decisions throughout delivery.
Facilitate working sessions, status reviews, and governance meetings to keep initiatives moving forward.
Provide clear and consistent updates to stakeholders and senior leaders.
Support the transition of completed work back into the business and confirm that agreed outcomes have been delivered.
Provide intake consulting and request support
Help business partners frame requests, define the business need, and determine the appropriate delivery path.
Distinguish between short-cycle requests and larger initiatives requiring formal planning, prioritization, and specialist support.
Develop presentations and materials that communicate project objectives, delivery status, decisions, risks, and outcomes.
Build and maintain reusable intake materials, project templates, KPI explainers, and business reference materials that improve consistency and reduce repeat requests.
Connect business, Analytics, and Data teams
Partner closely with the AVPs and Managers leading Analytics, Data, and Data Science to ensure work is scoped, prioritized, and handed off effectively.
Build strong domain knowledge across CTR, Mark’s, SportChek, Merchandising, Marketing, Customer Strategy, Digital, and Triangle.
Identify recurring requests, delivery challenges, and capability gaps through the intake process.
Feed patterns into planning and prioritization discussions to identify repeatable solutions, improved processes, or longer-term investments.
Promote consistent ways of working across business, Analytics, Data, and Technology teams.
Represent the intake and delivery function
Be the first call for senior COO and CCO leaders when they need support navigating an analytics, measurement, BI, or data request.
Provide clear guidance on request status, ownership, delivery approach, timelines, and next steps.
Present intake trends, portfolio status, delivery risks, capacity considerations, and program impact in business reviews and executive forums.
Ensure communication is concise, practical, and focused on the decisions or actions required.

What You Bring

Post-secondary education in Business, Project Management, Economics, Analytics, or a related discipline.
6+ years of experience in project management, business consulting, demand management, portfolio coordination, analytics operations, or a related role.
Demonstrated experience establishing or operating an intake, demand management, project governance, or centre of excellence function.
Strong experience defining business requirements, developing project plans, and coordinating work across multiple teams.
Proven ability to manage competing priorities, capacity constraints, delivery dependencies, and changes in scope.
Experience facilitating governance forums, prioritization discussions, working sessions, and executive updates.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to translate complex requests into clear scope, accountabilities, plans, and decisions.
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior business leaders and cross-functional partners.
General familiarity with analytics, BI, measurement, and data environments sufficient to support effective intake, scoping, and delivery coordination.
Project management certification or equivalent practical experience is an asset.

We may use artificial intelligence tools as part of our recruitment process to assist in the initial screening of resumes. All hiring decisions, including candidate evaluation, selection, and disposition, are made by human recruiters.

With more than 90 Owned Brands, over 1,600 retail locations, financial services, exemplary e-commerce capabilities, and exciting market-leading merchandising strategies. We dream big and work as one to innovate with purpose for our customers at every level of our business, investing in new technologies and products, and doubling down on top talent to drive the company forward. jobs.title: Field Operations - Operations Director
jobs.description:
Job Profile – Operations Director

We take care of those dedicated to taking care of animals.

VetStrategy is Canada's leading veterinary network, with over 360 hospitals and clinics and more than 5,500 veterinary professionals across the country. As part of IVC Evidensia, we support veterinary teams with the resources, expertise and operational leadership they need to deliver exceptional care and build thriving practices.

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Operations Director. This key leadership role is responsible for ensuring operational excellence across multiple veterinary practices, driving efficiency, and fostering a culture of accountability and high performance. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in operations management, exceptional leadership skills, and a proven track record of successfully managing multiple locations. The Operations Director works closely with Regional Medical Directors and corporate leaders to consistent delivery of best-in-class care, ensuring our practices embody and operate in alignment with VetStrategy’s values and Leadership Behaviours.

Work Location:
Hamilton/Niagara, ON. This is a regionally based role requiring regular travel across assigned veterinary practices. Flexibility to work remotely when not required on-site.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership and Team Management

Lead a team of Practice Managers, taking accountability for their delivery of business and people results
Build a high-performing team by driving accountability by setting clear expectations, providing regular coaching and feedback
Be an inspiring and accessible leader, building followership with practitioners and clinic colleagues across all locations
Foster a cohesive team environment through engagement activities and active change management.
Lead by example in fostering a positive work environment, encouraging collaboration and continuous improvement.
Partner with Regional Medical Directors to support communication with clinical teams on delivery of medical information.
Ensure positive resolution of escalated employee relations issues through collaboration with the People Operations Team
Maintain a strong presence within the district through frequent communication and visits.
Support the successful integration of new practices within the district through active engagement with Integrations team throughout the onboarding process.
Engage with Regional Medical Directors to ensure that new-to-network and new graduate veterinarians are integrating well and being set up for success by ensuring action plans are in place.

Drive Operational Excellence

Monitor and analyze key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify areas for improvement and create business plans to support those enhancements.
Develop and implement strategic plans to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness across assigned district.
Oversee the execution of operational initiatives to enhance patient care and client service.
Ensure consistent implementation of standard operating procedures (SOPs) within district.
Deepen capabilities of the team through best-practice sharing and coaching to embed a customer service, data driven and growth mindset

Financial Management

Oversee the creation and management of district practice budgets, ensuring financial targets are met.
Analyze district financial performance, drawing insight and taking action in response to trends.
Work with marketing teams to drive client acquisition and retention.
Ensure cost-effectiveness with resources and operational processes while maintaining high service standards and financial health.
Investment in practices: Identify and support the execution of investments in refurbishments, facilities, equipment, and technology so that practices provide the best possible care for patients.

Strategic Initiatives

Lead and collaborate on cross-functional projects to develop and implement strategic initiatives aimed at enhancing the financial performance of the business.
Lead the implementation of strategic initiatives and ensure alignment with the organization's goals and objectives within the district.
Communicate corporate policies and procedures to Practice Managers, ensuring understanding and compliance.
Monitor the effectiveness of corporate initiatives and provide feedback for continuous improvement.
Identify opportunities for business growth, including new services and marketing initiatives.

Compliance and Safety

Ensure all practices comply with relevant regulations, standards, and safety protocols.
Partner with Regional Medical Directors respond to adverse events, ensuring reporting and appropriate action are taken in response.
Include Regional Medical Directors in regular district meetings with Practice Managers to review and discuss clinical compliance and safety, updates to provincial regulations.
Review and evaluate Continuing Education (“CE”) approval decisions made by Practice Managers, ensuring practice teams are focused on learning that contributes to personal growth while elevating our practice.

Marketing & Client Relations

Lead the evaluation of local market assessments and promotions to identify opportunities for growth.
Work closely with the Marketing team to develop targeted marketing strategies based on local market assessments.
Ensure the successful execution of network-wide promotions, aligning them with local needs and preferences.
Collaborate with the national marketing team to exchange ideas and initiatives, fostering a cohesive marketing approach
Resolve escalated client relations issues to a positive end, engaging the Regional Medical Director where required.

Key Qualifications

Leadership Experience: Minimum of 7 years of experience in a management role, preferably in human or veterinary healthcare.
Education: Bachelor's degree in business administration, healthcare management, or a related field preferred.
Financial Acumen: Thorough understanding of financial management, including budgeting and financial reporting.
Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting formal business plans.
Organizational Skills: Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
Conflict Resolution: Demonstrated ability to effectively resolve conflicts within a team, utilizing strong interpersonal and communication skills to mediate disputes and foster a collaborative work environment
Client-Focused: A commitment to providing high-quality customer service and improving the overall client experience.
Critical Thinking: Proven ability to analyze complex situations, identify key issues, and develop effective solutions. Demonstrates strong problem-solving skills and the capacity to make well-informed decisions under pressure.
IT Proficiency: Comfortable with Microsoft Office, and other digital tools for managing administrative tasks.

Demonstrates our Leadership Behaviours

Value (The Why)

Behaviour (The How)

Behaviour: Definition

We Care

Motivating

Show self-belief, build strong teams, motivate others to reach their potential.

We Care

Resilient

Effectively manage their own well-being and that of others, quickly recover from challenges, and learn from mistakes.

We Dare

Results-driven

Relentlessly seek to improve business performance, act decisively, drive progress through clear expectations.

We Dare

Lead for the future

Balance the perfect and pragmatic, prioritise long-term progress, drive sustainable innovation.

We Share

Humble

Act with integrity, earn trust through transparency, pursue personal development.

We Share

Collaborative

Stretch outside their own area of expertise to drive performance, happy to learn from others, inspire teams through great communication.

jobs.title: Director, IT Application Audit
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

The Director, IT Application Audit
is responsible for the oversight and delivery of risk-based internal audits across the Business Group Chief Information Officer (CIO) application portfolio and technology in Canada and the United States, and when needed in Asia. The role provides independent assurance and advisory support over business applications, data, digital delivery, enabling platforms and associated technology and cyber risk management practices. The scope includes First and Second Line activities and support for integrated business audits with significant technology components.

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, IT Audit, the Director leads assigned members of a geographically dispersed audit team and is accountable for high-quality audit delivery, stakeholder relationships, people development and continuous improvement of audit practices.

What You Will Be Doing

The scope of responsibilities includes for assigned areas the operational delivery of all IT audit work, audit plan development and coverage, IT audit universe risk assessments to ensure the adequacy of audit coverage of key risks, as well as relationship management with clients and management of the audit team.
Identify emerging and heightened risk related to technology and cyber security in applications and technology processes, digital transformation and modernization, AI and data.
Contribute to the development of Audit strategy and direction, and talent initiatives.
Continuously improve audit delivery and quality through increased use of AI, data analytics and innovation.
Plan and direct audits and special engagements following Sun Life’s Audit methodology; deliver audit reports and findings that clearly articulate the position of risks and issues.
Provide subject matter expertise as it relates to technology, cyber and information risk management processes to other audit teams.
Provide leadership in discussions of risk assessment, internal control and audit findings with clients.
Actively stay engaged in the latest technologies, regulations and cyber trends.
Manage multiple engagements and priorities concurrently, including scope, resourcing, milestones, quality review, stakeholder communication and issue escalation.
Influence management to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of operations, risk management practices and the control environment with respect to technology, cyber and information risk management.
Lead an audit team with a focus on building and maintaining a high-performing team of auditors, including the recruitment, administration, development and retention of staff through strong leadership and coaching.

What You Need to Succeed

6-8+ years of leadership experience in IT, IT Audit, or related risk management or governance/control functions.
University degree or equivalent experience, plus recognized auditing (e.g., CISA, CPA, CIA), or security (e.g., CISSP) designations/certifications.
Previous people management experience, with demonstrated employee engagement results.
This role is based in Toronto and the individual is expected to work in a hybrid environment (virtual and in the office). Occasional travel to the US and rarely to Asia may be required.
In-depth knowledge of audit methodologies, system development methodologies, control frameworks, risk practices and regulatory requirements.
Exceptional understanding of application development & maintenance, technology and cyber processes, risks and controls.
In-depth knowledge of the latest application technology and security trends, best practices and industry standards.
Proficiency in cyber security risk and control frameworks and information risk management frameworks.
Strong working knowledge of risks affecting the insurance industry and financial institutions.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and succinctly and effectively deliver key messages verbally and in writing.
Effective listener who remains open and receptive to various viewpoints.
Confident presenter and facilitator with strong interpersonal and leadership skills to work with senior management at all levels.
Effective influencer and negotiator with the ability to effectively manage and resolve conflicts across all levels of management.
Professional presence and the ability to navigate through a matrix organization.
Critical thinker who can assess risk and controls and identify issues.
Flexible, organized and able to effectively manage multiple engagements and priorities concurrently.
Strategic thinker who can see and share the big picture while retaining attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities to use AI and data analytics to enhance the depth and breadth of audit coverage.
Demonstrated ability to work and lead effectively in diverse environments and cultures across multiple office locations.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Senior Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP, Orthopedics
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP, Orthopedics based in Canada .

The Senior Director will provide strategic and operational leadership for enterprise SAP Supply Chain solutions across a complex global technology environment. This role will oversee multiple SAP ECC and S/4HANA instances, guiding critical technology initiatives associated with a major business separation, including Day 1 readiness, transition services, and eventual system consolidation. Working closely with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, and IT leaders, the successful candidate will ensure that ERP capabilities support business priorities, regulatory obligations, and operational continuity. The position combines enterprise architecture, large-scale transformation, application delivery, and financial governance with responsibility for a high-performing global organization. It also offers the opportunity to modernize ERP operations through AI, automation, standardization, and continuous improvement.

Accountabilities

Lead the end-to-end strategy, architecture, delivery, and operations of SAP ERP Supply Chain capabilities across multiple SAP ECC and S/4HANA instances, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities.
Oversee SAP systems supporting business separation milestones, including Day 1 readiness, transition activities throughout the Transition Services Agreement (TSA) period, and consolidation into S/4HANA to support TSA exit.
Prioritize regulatory, operational, and strategic initiatives to maximize business value while meeting critical separation and transformation milestones.
Establish and maintain SAP ERP governance frameworks, including architecture standards, investment planning, budgets, and technology operating models.
Manage relationships with SAP providers, system integrators, managed services partners, and strategic technology vendors, overseeing licensing strategies, contracts, and service performance.
Transform and support ERP capabilities across Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Quality, ensuring compliance with business priorities and applicable regulatory requirements.
Drive the adoption of AI and automation to modernize ERP operations at scale, including code remediation, automated testing, and operational efficiency improvements.
Ensure the integrity, security, and regulatory compliance of SAP ERP solutions, including data governance and cybersecurity controls.
Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing global technology organization, bringing together internal teams, onshore and offshore resources, and strategic partners.
Maintain strong financial oversight of technology investments and operating expenditure while promoting continuous improvement, innovation, and standardization across the SAP ecosystem.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related discipline is required. A master's degree, MBA, MS, or equivalent qualification is preferred.
12–14 years of progressive experience planning, designing, delivering, and supporting enterprise SAP business applications.
Extensive experience leading, architecting, and supporting SAP ERP environments, including SAP ECC, SAP S/4HANA, satellite SAP solutions, and integrations with non-SAP systems.
Demonstrated expertise in SAP application delivery, including development, release and change management, security, archiving, data migration, and landscape coordination.
Proven success leading large-scale global technology programs and complex enterprise transformations, particularly SAP S/4HANA migrations.
Strong knowledge of Supply Chain ERP processes and solutions, including planning, manufacturing, distribution, logistics, and quality management.
Experience working in highly regulated Life Sciences environments, with a solid understanding of compliance, validation, and data integrity requirements.
Demonstrated people leadership capabilities, including building diverse, inclusive, high-performing teams and establishing offshore Global Capability Center (GCC) delivery teams.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical reasoning, fact-based decision-making, stakeholder management, and communication skills.
Experience supporting complex medical device supply chains and manufacturing environments, including specialized processes such as loaner equipment, servicing, and repairs, is preferred.
Experience leading large-scale business separations and divestitures through Day 1 readiness and TSA exit is an advantage.
Experience managing global system integrators and strategic technology vendors, as well as multi-year technology budgets, is preferred.
Change leadership experience in large, matrixed organizations is desirable.
Familiarity with SAP Center of Excellence (COE) platform services is preferred, including BASIS administration, ABAP and SAP IS development, SAP BTP, release and transport management, landscape coordination, security, archiving, and data migration.
English proficiency is required. Certifications in IT, SAP, Supply Chain, or program management, such as PMP or ITIL, are preferred.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 20% is required.

Benefits

Anticipated annual base salary range of $187,000–$320,850.
Eligibility to participate in a pension plan and a 401(k) savings plan, subject to applicable plan terms.
Eligibility for participation in a long-term incentive program.
Vacation: 120 hours per calendar year.
Sick leave: 40 hours per calendar year, with higher allowances for eligible employees in Colorado and Washington.
Paid holidays: 13 days per calendar year, including floating holidays.
Work, Personal, and Family Time: Up to 40 hours per calendar year.
Parental leave: 480 hours within one year of the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child.
Bereavement leave: Up to 240 hours for an immediate family member and 40 hours for an extended family member per calendar year.
Caregiver leave: 80 hours within a rolling 52-week period.
Volunteer leave: 32 hours per calendar year.
Military spouse time off: 80 hours per calendar year.
Fully remote work arrangement, subject to applicable location and employment conditions.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
This role is ideally based in Toronto with hybrid working in our offices but we are open to candidates in other parts of Canada. There is some travel involved in the role, trips to Australia once per quarter and other ad hoc trips as required.

Fleet Space Technologies is a frontier technology company building the clearest 3D understanding of a mineral system before the next capital, targeting or drilling decision. Led by high-quality hard-rock seismic, Fleet integrates geology, geophysics, drilling data, geochemistry and mineralogy with geoscience expertise and machine learning, turning complex subsurface data into actionable insight.

We're looking for a Chief of Staff to report to & assist our COO who is based in Toronto to remove bottlenecks, improve operational processes, create GTM strategies for new regions and anything else that helps Fleet and our COO reach their goals.

You'll be the person Fleet Space looks to when we need to launch in a country we don't yet operate in, and the person who builds the planning rhythm, shared definitions and capacity forecasts that let us scale with rigour across the globe.

This is a builder's seat, not a VP role with a large organisation underneath it. You'll lead a small team of two to four and work with line leaders of every department and you'll personally do much of the work rather than just design it.

You'll start with training & onboarding on the ground in Australia, on the factory floor and out on a live survey in the field to understand our operations from end to end.

Adelaide, South Australia is our Global HQ, so some early mornings and late evenings are common but you are also given a lot of autonomy and flexibility around where and when you work best.

What you'll do

Build and own our country entry playbook: customs clearance and temporary imports, local agent and partner selection, entity versus partner decisions, permits, visas, crew mobilisation and field HSE
Know when a country needs a partner, when it needs an entity, and when we should walk away
Work alongside our joint venture partners on delivery, without owning their commercials
Connect manufacturing, supply chain, deployment and refurbishment as one system, connecting factory output to field demand so we are never building blind or short
Own the Geode refurbishment loop: turn time, attrition, yield and the units that get stranded in country
Set our spares, consumables and logistics strategy across regions, and manage supplier and contract manufacturer performance where it touches delivery
Design and personally run the COO's operating & reporting cadence: annual, quarterly, monthly and weekly planning, with a clear owner for every input
Create one shared definition of a survey, a deployment, a delay and a completion, and run operating reviews that surface the truth early rather than confirm it late
Build the demand and capacity model for crews, Geodes, satellites, field engineers and geoscience interpretation, turning the commercial pipeline into headcount and hardware plans our leadership can plan against
Track forecast against actual every quarter and keep making it better

What we are looking for

Chief of Staff or similar roles with a background in Operations, ideally within startup/scale up tech companies with a hardware component or mining/mineral exploration industry
Strengths in Forecasting, Executive level reporting, GTM strategy development & building out various models, systems and frameworks
Experience in companies with hardware products with responsibilities across manufacturing, supply chain, deployment, service or refurbishment
A self starter, someone that can identify and prioritise the work rather than wait for a task to be given to them
8+ years in senior operations leadership positions, with recent experience executing & delivering projects yourself rather than only overseeing others but capable of people management as well
A background in mining, mining services, geophysical survey, drilling, oilfield services or resources technology is a plus
Experience across at least three of Latin America, the Middle East, Africa, Central Asia and Australia
Start/Scale-up experience, you understand the pace and variety in the role and don’t need or want the slow corporate world
Willingness to travel globally
Professional fluency in a second language - particularly Spanish, French or Arabic - would be a real plus

About Fleet Space

Fleet Space Technologies is an Australian frontier technology company building the clearest 3D understanding of a mineral system before the next capital, targeting or drilling decision: led by high-quality hard-rock seismic, Fleet integrates geology, geophysics, drilling data, geochemistry and mineralogy with geoscience expertise and machine learning, turning complex subsurface data into actionable insight.

Founded in 2015 in Adelaide, South Australia, Fleet Space Technologies set out to bring the engineering rigour, connected hardware and computational power of the space industry to help solve mining’s hardest problems, and deliver drill predictions that stand up against ground truth.

Company Culture

As a company, we are revolutionising the exploration of new worlds with advanced space technology to build a more prosperous future for humanity.

As a culture, we are ambitious, innovative, and collaborative and we put our customers first in everything that we do.

Our company values guide us to our North Star of ambitious, collaborative success: AD ASTRA ("To the Stars!")

Add Value:
Obsessively add value for our customers
Drive Excellence:
Benchmark against the best
Agile Action:
Take Action. Independent, fast, frugal action
Seek Truth:
Be curious. Explore
Take Responsibility:
Make decisions and own them
Radical Ideas:
We are unique. We do things differently
Always Deliver:
We always find a way to get it done on time

Our Benefits Include

We have an extremely flexible work culture, with a mix of onsite, hybrid and remote workers who take time for school runs, exercise and appointments. With global teams hours can vary butiIt's about getting the work done, not what time you are at your desk.
Equity (ESOP) grants.
20 days of annual leave + 10 extra Wellness days per year.
Learning budgets.
Access to confidential Psychologist appointments via our Employee Assistance Program.
Plenty of opportunity to be part of an amazing STEM program to create the next generation of explorers.

Fleet is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Fleet is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, colour, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

new_jobs.title: Chief of Staff
new_jobs.description:
This role is ideally based in Toronto with hybrid working in our offices but we are open to candidates in other parts of Canada. There is some travel involved in the role, trips to Australia once per quarter and other ad hoc trips as required.

Fleet Space Technologies is a frontier technology company building the clearest 3D understanding of a mineral system before the next capital, targeting or drilling decision. Led by high-quality hard-rock seismic, Fleet integrates geology, geophysics, drilling data, geochemistry and mineralogy with geoscience expertise and machine learning, turning complex subsurface data into actionable insight.

We're looking for a Chief of Staff to report to & assist our COO who is based in Toronto to remove bottlenecks, improve operational processes, create GTM strategies for new regions and anything else that helps Fleet and our COO reach their goals.

You'll be the person Fleet Space looks to when we need to launch in a country we don't yet operate in, and the person who builds the planning rhythm, shared definitions and capacity forecasts that let us scale with rigour across the globe.

This is a builder's seat, not a VP role with a large organisation underneath it. You'll lead a small team of two to four and work with line leaders of every department and you'll personally do much of the work rather than just design it.

You'll start with training & onboarding on the ground in Australia, on the factory floor and out on a live survey in the field to understand our operations from end to end.

Adelaide, South Australia is our Global HQ, so some early mornings and late evenings are common but you are also given a lot of autonomy and flexibility around where and when you work best.

What you'll do

Build and own our country entry playbook: customs clearance and temporary imports, local agent and partner selection, entity versus partner decisions, permits, visas, crew mobilisation and field HSE
Know when a country needs a partner, when it needs an entity, and when we should walk away
Work alongside our joint venture partners on delivery, without owning their commercials
Connect manufacturing, supply chain, deployment and refurbishment as one system, connecting factory output to field demand so we are never building blind or short
Own the Geode refurbishment loop: turn time, attrition, yield and the units that get stranded in country
Set our spares, consumables and logistics strategy across regions, and manage supplier and contract manufacturer performance where it touches delivery
Design and personally run the COO's operating & reporting cadence: annual, quarterly, monthly and weekly planning, with a clear owner for every input
Create one shared definition of a survey, a deployment, a delay and a completion, and run operating reviews that surface the truth early rather than confirm it late
Build the demand and capacity model for crews, Geodes, satellites, field engineers and geoscience interpretation, turning the commercial pipeline into headcount and hardware plans our leadership can plan against
Track forecast against actual every quarter and keep making it better

What we are looking for

Chief of Staff or similar roles with a background in Operations, ideally within startup/scale up tech companies with a hardware component or mining/mineral exploration industry
Strengths in Forecasting, Executive level reporting, GTM strategy development & building out various models, systems and frameworks
Experience in companies with hardware products with responsibilities across manufacturing, supply chain, deployment, service or refurbishment
A self starter, someone that can identify and prioritise the work rather than wait for a task to be given to them
8+ years in senior operations leadership positions, with recent experience executing & delivering projects yourself rather than only overseeing others but capable of people management as well
A background in mining, mining services, geophysical survey, drilling, oilfield services or resources technology is a plus
Experience across at least three of Latin America, the Middle East, Africa, Central Asia and Australia
Start/Scale-up experience, you understand the pace and variety in the role and don’t need or want the slow corporate world
Willingness to travel globally
Professional fluency in a second language - particularly Spanish, French or Arabic - would be a real plus

About Fleet Space

Fleet Space Technologies is an Australian frontier technology company building the clearest 3D understanding of a mineral system before the next capital, targeting or drilling decision: led by high-quality hard-rock seismic, Fleet integrates geology, geophysics, drilling data, geochemistry and mineralogy with geoscience expertise and machine learning, turning complex subsurface data into actionable insight.

Founded in 2015 in Adelaide, South Australia, Fleet Space Technologies set out to bring the engineering rigour, connected hardware and computational power of the space industry to help solve mining’s hardest problems, and deliver drill predictions that stand up against ground truth.

Company Culture

As a company, we are revolutionising the exploration of new worlds with advanced space technology to build a more prosperous future for humanity.

As a culture, we are ambitious, innovative, and collaborative and we put our customers first in everything that we do.

Our company values guide us to our North Star of ambitious, collaborative success: AD ASTRA ("To the Stars!")

Add Value:
Obsessively add value for our customers
Drive Excellence:
Benchmark against the best
Agile Action:
Take Action. Independent, fast, frugal action
Seek Truth:
Be curious. Explore
Take Responsibility:
Make decisions and own them
Radical Ideas:
We are unique. We do things differently
Always Deliver:
We always find a way to get it done on time

Our Benefits Include

We have an extremely flexible work culture, with a mix of onsite, hybrid and remote workers who take time for school runs, exercise and appointments. With global teams hours can vary butiIt's about getting the work done, not what time you are at your desk.
Equity (ESOP) grants.
20 days of annual leave + 10 extra Wellness days per year.
Learning budgets.
Access to confidential Psychologist appointments via our Employee Assistance Program.
Plenty of opportunity to be part of an amazing STEM program to create the next generation of explorers.

Fleet is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Fleet is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, colour, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
